messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For Esperanto, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Requirements (ONE Markdown table): - Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] - In [Target Requirement], make comparative direction unambiguous and add a 1-line literal back-translation check. Output: ONLY the table; no extra prose.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Requirement | |-------------|----------------------|--------------------| | Tant' | “so” – intensifier of the following adjective | Render as **tiel** (adverb) modifying the predicate adjective; back‑translation: *“tiel amara” → “so bitter.”* | | è | Copular verb linking implicit subject “it” to predicate | Use Esperanto **estas** (present copula); back‑translation: *“estas” → “is.”* | | amara | Predicate adjective meaning “bitter” | Use **amara** (adjective) predicated of the subject; back‑translation: *“amara” → “bitter.”* | | che | Comparative subordinator introducing the benchmark clause | Translate with **ol** (comparative conjunction); back‑translation: *“ol” → “that … is.”* | | poco | Adverb meaning “little” that qualifies the degree of the comparative | Place **iom** before the comparative adjective; back‑translation: *“iom” → “a little.”* | | è (in comparative clause) | Copular verb linking “death” to the comparative predicate | Use **estas** again; back‑translation: *“estas” → “is.”* | | più | Comparative adverb “more” (degree of bitterness) | Use **pli** + adjective (**pli amara**) to express “more bitter”; back‑translation: *“pli amara” → “more bitter.”* | | morte | Noun “death”, subject of the comparative clause | Render as **mort** (noun) with appropriate case (nominative); back‑translation: *“mort” → “death.”* | | ma | Coordinating conjunction indicating contrast | Translate as **sed**; back‑translation: *“sed” → “but.”* | | per | Preposition marking purpose of the infinitive | Use **por** + infinitive; back‑translation: *“por” → “in order to.”* | | trattar | Infinitive “to treat / discuss” | Render as **trakti** (infinitive); back‑translation: *“trakti” → “to treat.”* | | del | Contraction of “di + il” → preposition “of the” | Use **de la**; back‑translation: *“de la” → “of the.”* | | ben | Abstract noun “good” | Render as **bono** (noun) or **bono** as a concept; back‑translation: *“bono” → “good.”* | | ch'i' | Relative pronoun + personal pronoun “that I” | Translate as **kiun mi** (relative clause) or **kiun mi** depending on function; back‑translation: *“kiun mi” → “that I.”* | | vi | Locative adverb “there” | Use **tie**; back‑translation: *“tie” → “there.”* | | trovai | Simple past “I found” (historic) | Render as **trovis** (past tense of **trovi**); back‑translation: *“trovis” → “found.”* | | dirò | Future “I will say/tell” | Use **diros** (future of **diri**); back‑translation: *“diros” → “will tell.”* | | de | Preposition “of” introducing the upcoming domain | Use **pri** (about) or **de** depending on nuance; here **pri** fits “about”; back‑translation: *“pri” → “of/about.”* | | l'altre | Definite article + adjective “the other” (plural) | Render as **la aliaj** (plural adjective + article); back‑translation: *“la aliaj” → “the other.”* | | cose | Noun “things” (plural) | Use **aĵoj** (plural noun) or **aĵoj**; back‑translation: *“aĵoj” → “things.”* | | ch'i' (second occurrence) | Relative pronoun + personal pronoun “that I” | Same as above: **kiun mi**; back‑translation: *“kiun mi” → “that I.”* | | v'ho | Perfect auxiliary “have … there” (locative clitic) | Use **mi havas tie** (auxiliary + locative) or **mi jam vidis tie**; for perfect of “see” we use **mi jam vidis tie**; back‑translation: *“mi jam vidis tie” → “have … there (seen).”* | | scorte | Past participle “seen” agreeing with plural feminine | Render as **viditaj** (past participle agreeing with **aĵoj**) or simply **vidis** in a finite clause; back‑translation: *“viditaj” → “seen.”* |
**Comparative Direction Note:** In the clause “death is a little more bitter,” the Esperanto construction must be **mort estas iom pli amara ol X**, where **X** is the antecedent (the “it” of line 7). The presence of **iom** guarantees the “little” qualifier, and **pli … ol** makes the comparative direction explicit (death > X).

### Step 3: Pre-assembled Lexical Inventory Create placeable Esperanto components for Step 4. Output ONLY bullet list; ONE LINE per bullet. - Line <ID>: <Phrase 1> / <Phrase 2> / <Phrase 3> Where <ID> is the leading integer at the start of the source line. Hook: each phrase must satisfy the Step 2 Requirements table for that line (including the literal back-translation checks). Rules: Each phrase is directly placeable in the final line (no glue-only fragments). Must keep the line’s main predicate + any required linkage (result/purpose/relative); do not output only a subordinate fragment. Avoid embedding clause-linking connectors inside a phrase; keep phrases as clean, placeable propositions and let Step 4 add any necessary linking function-words/morphology. For comparatives, preserve direction and include comparator/degree in the phrase. No punctuation characters inside phrases; keep phrases short; no newlines.

- Line 7: tiel amara ol iom pli amara mort / tiel amara ol mort estas iom pli amara / tiel amara ol iom pli amara estas mort - Line 8: sed por trakti de la bono kiun mi trovis tie / sed por trakti la bonon kiun mi trovis tie / sed por trakti pri la bono kiun mi trovis tie - Line 9: diros pri la aliaj aĵoj kiujn mi jam vidis tie / diros pri la aliaj aferoj kiujn mi jam vidis tie / diros pri la aliaj objektoj kiujn mi jam vidis tie

### Step 4: Slot-Based Syntactic Assembly Assemble Step3 components into Esperanto lines; keep the same number of lines. Use Step3 Final Form as contiguous substrings; reorder within-line as needed. If simple concatenation is ungrammatical or produces a predicate-clash, you MAY insert only function-words and/or inflectional morphology needed for grammatical joining; do NOT add new content words. When adding linking function-words/morphology, match the relation implied by the source line (result/purpose/relative) and do NOT turn it into a contrast relation unless the source explicitly contrasts. Semantic completeness: each Target Text MUST express the full Locked Meaning for that Source Line; do NOT drop the main predicate when the line contains a main predicate + linked clause. Punctuation: copy ONLY end punctuation from the source line to the END of Target Text; add NO internal punctuation. For each source line output ONLY this block (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Line Inventory: - <copy the phrases you chose from Step 3 for this line> Assembly Notes: - If you inserted any function-words/morphology for joining, list them briefly. Target Text: <assembled target line> If you forgot a necessary phrase from Step 3: re-insert it (no new content words).

**Source Line:** 7 Tant' è amara che poco è più morte;
**Line Inventory:** - tiel amara ol mort estas iom pli amara
**Assembly Notes:** - No additional function‑words needed; the phrase already contains the main predicate and the comparative clause.
**Target Text:** tiel amara ol mort estas iom pli amara;
---
**Source Line:** 8 ma per trattar del ben ch'i' vi trovai,
**Line Inventory:** - sed por trakti la bonon kiun mi trovis tie
**Assembly Notes:** - “sed” supplies the contrastive “ma”; “por” supplies the purpose preposition required by “per”.
**Target Text:** sed por trakti la bonon kiun mi trovis tie,
---
**Source Line:** 9 dirò de l'altre cose ch'i' v'ho scorte.
**Line Inventory:** - diros pri la aliaj aĵoj kiujn mi jam vidis tie
**Assembly Notes:** - No extra words needed; the phrase includes the future verb, the preposition, the determiner, and the relative clause.
**Target Text:** diros pri la aliaj aĵoj kiujn mi jam vidis tie.

### Step 5: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check Verify each Step4 line vs Reference Translation + Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within the line; re-insert only Step4 Missing; fix function-word/morphology anywhere; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation rule: do NOT introduce new internal punctuation; only keep the end punctuation transferred from the source line. Per line output bullets with EXACT fields: - Line #: <ID> - Target Text (from Step 4): <...> - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): <...> - Reference Translation (line-aligned): <...> - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> - If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text: <...> End Punct: compare last non-whitespace char of Target Text vs Source Line. Line # rule: <ID> is the leading integer at the start of that Source Line. After all lines: if any FAIL, label final as UNVERIFIED and list failing Line # values. Output final Esperanto text in ONE code block, line by line.

- Line #: 7 - Target Text (from Step 4): tiel amara ol mort estas iom pli amara; - Back-Translation (literal): “so bitter than death is a little more bitter;” - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): So bitter is it that death is little more. - Checks: End Punct **OK**, Coverage **FAIL**, Meaning Drift **FAIL**, Comparative Orientation **FAIL**, Hallucination **OK** - Corrected Target Text: tiel amara ke mort estas iom pli amara;
- Line #: 8 - Target Text (from Step 4): sed por trakti la bonon kiun mi trovis tie, - Back-Translation (literal): “but to treat the good which I found there,” - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): But in order to treat of the good that there I found, - Checks: End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK**
- Line #: 9 - Target Text (from Step 4): diros pri la aliaj aĵoj kiujn mi jam vidis tie. - Back-Translation (literal): “will say about the other things which I have already seen there.” - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): I will tell of the other things that I have seen there. - Checks: End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK**
**UNVERIFIED** – failing lines: 7
```esperanto tiel amara ke mort estas iom pli amara; sed por trakti la bonon kiun mi trovis tie, diros pri la aliaj aĵoj kiujn mi jam vidis tie. ```
